Night Tennis

Night Tennis in Toronto

A 2016 City report put public court hours at 8 a.m. to dusk, or 10 p.m. where a court has lights. Measured from sunset, the 10 p.m. closing gives lit courts 57 extra minutes on June 21, just over two hours on September 1, three on October 1 and almost four on October 31. However from November 1st, when the clocks go back, we lose 4 to 5 hours of playtime on courts without lights.

Court of the Month / 02

From a Gated Community to a Wooded Ravine

Fun FactLine 1 tunnels run beneath the park
New playgroundSummer 2027

Located in Midtown, just south of Eglinton Avenue West, Cedarvale Park was once envisioned to be an exclusive gated community by Sir Henry Pellat, the financier that built the Casa Loma, only to be halted by WWII and the great depression. The valley was then slated for the Spadina Expressway, only to be finally cleared in the 1970s for the subway tunnel that now runs beneath it. The forest has since grown back, as the southern part of the park drops into a wooded ravine, with an off-leash dog arena, a trail that runs to St.Clair West Station and a cattail wetland farther south.

The four tennis courts are in the open north end, with Phil White Arena and a cricket pitch. Among the 67 courts our members name, Cedarvale is home to 19 of our members.

A club ran here before 1999, when a City report noted that the outdoor clubs at Cedarvale and Smythe parks had been cancelled after memberships declined. In the spring of 2012, a group calling itself the Cedarvale Tennis Academy proposed running Cedarvale Park’s four public tennis courts as a membership club, with fees to pay for upkeep. Neighbours objected, in a fight to keep the courts public, Toronto Life reported.

Eglinton West station became Cedarvale station on December 7, 2025. Line 5 Eglinton opened there on February 8, 2026, so the station is now where Line 1 meets Line 5. Players coming from the south can take the ravine trail, which links St. Clair West station to the north end of the park.

Friends of Cedarvale is a small neighbourhood group dedicated to maintaining and improving Cedarvale Park and Ravine. The group began in 2012. Volunteers run Saturday stewardship sessions that pull invasive plants, a litter pickup team and guided nature walks.

NIGHT TENNIS

A Brief Look at the Landscape of Night Tennis in Toronto

A 2016 City report put the tennis season at about April 1 to October 31. On the last day of that season the sun sets in Toronto at 6:10 p.m. The clocks go back the next day, and by the second week of November it sets before five.

The same report put public court hours at 8 a.m. to dusk, or 10 p.m. where a court has lights. Measured from sunset, the 10 p.m. closing gives lit courts 57 extra minutes on June 21, just over two hours on September 1, three on October 1 and almost four on October 31.

  1. The City’s 2017 Parks and Recreation Facilities Master Plan counted 602 tennis courts in 185 parks, about one court for every 4,800 residents. Of those, 339 are public courts and 263 are club courts, which the City reports put at 61 not-for-profit clubs. The plan found an oversupply of public courts and set no target for adding more. It still recommended up to 20 new courts over 20 years in growth areas without court access, naming Downtown and North Scarborough.

  2. The City’s 2025 to 2027 court improvements program which funds one park per ward covers 28 parks, with Cedarvale not among them. 24 programs have been completed. The City asked residents about lighting, fencing and surfaces. No park on the list shows lighting work. In the City’s survey of 19 parks, lighting was a top theme at 11, with at least 169 comments. Ramsden drew 45, High Park 35 and Norwood 24. At Ramsden, surfaces drew more than lighting, with 100 comments which is why the resurfacing was prioritized

  3. In our 2026 season review, 263 members named 67 Toronto courts as their preferred option with downtown-midtown covering 75% of our player base. Downtown has only one court with lights, Moss Park. The closest zone with night lights is the Etobicoke-Lakeshore, with 76% courts covered with lights, the second-highest share of lit public courts.

Level up your game

What is shadow practice?

Learn how to build perfect muscle memory, without a ball.

Shadow practice is the rehearsal of your swings and footwork through the air without an actual ball or opponent. You perform full, controlled strokes, focusing entirely on clean mechanics, smooth weight transfer, and proper balance.

Do it too fast and you’ll just repeat your bad habits; omit the footwork and you won’t build a realistic kinetic chain. Watch any pro pacing the back of the court before a match and you’ll see them visualizing and shadow-swinging through their strokes.

WatchShadow practice drill 1Shadow practice drill 2
Drill to try this week
The Mirror Freeze

Stand in front of a full-length mirror. Shadow-swing your forehand or backhand at 25% speed, and physically freeze your body exactly at the contact point. Check that your racket face is flush, your knees are bent, and your non-dominant hand is balanced. Do 20 controlled swings per side to lock in the feeling

The Tie Break

Trivia & a mini crossword

Trivia

How many players have gone on to win a Grand Slam after entering the main draw as a wildcard?

1
2
Across
1. A big overhead shot (5)
Down
1. Rotation on the ball (4)
2. A serve your opponent can’t touch (3)

Answers: Trivia, two: Goran Ivanisevic (Wimbledon 2001) and Kim Clijsters (US Open 2009). Across, 1 SMASH. Down, 1 SPIN · 2 ACE.
